title: Conditionals
subtitle: if, elif, else — make decisions in code
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: Programs need to make decisions — show a different message if the user is logged in, charge a different price for members, warn if a number is negative.
whyItExists.solution: if/elif/else lets Python take different paths based on conditions. Indentation (4 spaces) defines the code block that runs when a condition is true.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Any time behavior depends on a condition. Input validation, access control, game logic, data classification.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: If you have more than 5-6 elif branches, consider a dictionary dispatch or match statement (Python 3.10+).

explainModes.beginner: if asks a question. If the answer is True, it runs the indented code below. elif is 'else if' — another question if the first was False. else is the fallback — runs if nothing else matched.
explainModes.simple: Python uses indentation (4 spaces) instead of curly braces. if condition: / elif condition: / else: — only one branch runs. Ternary: value_if_true if condition else value_if_false. match (Python 3.10+) for pattern matching.
explainModes.standard: Conditions can be any expression that evaluates to truthy or falsy. Truthy: non-zero numbers, non-empty strings/lists/dicts. Falsy: 0, 0.0, '', [], {}, None, False. Short-circuit: conditions in and/or chains stop evaluating as soon as the result is determined. Nested ifs should be kept shallow — prefer early returns.
explainModes.technical: Python's if is a compound statement — header (if expr:) followed by a suite (indented body). The condition is evaluated left-to-right with short-circuit. Python 3.10's structural pattern matching (match/case) is more powerful than switch: it matches on value, type, structure, and guards. isinstance(x, int) is the idiomatic type check for branching on type.
explainModes.deepDive: Python has no switch statement before 3.10. match/case uses structural pattern matching (PEP 634) — not just equality: it can destructure tuples, lists, dicts, and class instances. Guards: case x if x > 0: — adds a condition. Python's if is an expression statement, not an expression — you can't use it inline. The ternary (conditional expression) is the inline alternative: x = a if cond else b.

content.code:
# ternary: value_if_true if condition else value_if_false
age = 20
status = 'adult' if age >= 18 else 'minor'
print(status)   # adult

# Use in f-string
stock = 0
print(f'Item is {"in stock" if stock > 0 else "out of stock"}')
# → Item is out of stock

# Python 3.10+ — match/case (structural pattern matching)
command = 'quit'

match command:
    case 'quit':
        print('Quitting...')
    case 'help':
        print('Showing help...')
    case _:          # default (like else)
        print(f'Unknown command: {command}')

questions.question: In Python, how do you define a code block?
questions.explanation: Python uses indentation (typically 4 spaces) to define code blocks — not curly braces like JavaScript/Java. All lines in a block must be indented consistently. IndentationError means you got it wrong.

faq.q: Can I use tabs for indentation?
faq.a: Technically yes, but don't mix tabs and spaces — it causes IndentationError in Python 3. The standard (PEP 8) is 4 spaces. Configure your editor to insert 4 spaces when you press Tab.

faq.q: Is there a switch statement in Python?
faq.a: From Python 3.10+: yes, match/case (structural pattern matching). Before 3.10, use if/elif chains or a dictionary dispatch: {key: function} patterns.

examples: if response.status_code == 200: — check API success in every HTTP call
if user.is_admin: — permission checking in web frameworks
Ternary: label = 'you' if user == current_user else user.name
